findings.issue_text: BlockedEmail#should_block? (app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-16) performs a non-atomic load → mutate → full-save cycle, so concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email (the exact spam-wave scenario this feature targets) both load the row and overwrite each other, silently losing increments and causing match_count/last_match_at to undercount
The return value of record.save in should_block? is never checked, so a failed save (e.g., a validation failure on the BlockedEmail row) drops the statistics update with no error surfaced

Because the blocked-match statistics write happens inside validate_each, any flow that validates the same user more than once (valid? followed by save, admin screens, etc.) double-counts a single signup attempt

The client condition `result.errors.email && result.values` (create_account_controller.js:274-276) rejects the email for any server email error, not just 'blocked' — uniqueness ('has already been taken') and whitelist/blacklist ('not allowed from that email provider') failures also push the email into rejectedEmails, so the field permanently shows the generic user.email.invalid message while the actual reason only appears in the transient flash; worst case, a returning user who forgot they have an account is told their valid email is invalid rather than being directed to log in, and the address is hard-blocked client-side for the rest of the session

In lib/validators/email_validator.rb:17, the guard `if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` short-circuits: because presence/uniqueness validations run first, an email that is both blocked and already registered (or domain-rejected) never reaches should_block?, so match_count is never incremented and last_match_at stays stale — the guard conflates 'don't add a second error' with 'don't record the match'

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` in create_account_controller.js:17 is evaluated once at class-definition time and lives on the prototype, so every instance of the controller shares and mutates the same array via pushObject; if the controller is ever instantiated per-modal, instances cross-contaminate

rejectedEmails is never cleared on modal close, success, or reset, so a rejected email stays blocked client-side for the entire page session even after the underlying server condition is resolved (e.g., admin removes the block or the 'already taken' account is deleted) — the user sees 'invalid' for a perfectly usable address until a full page reload

The blocked-email lookup (app/models/blocked_email.rb:12) uses exact, case/whitespace-sensitive matching (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)`), unlike the case-insensitive regex used by the domain whitelist/blacklist it sits beside — an admin who blocks spammer@x.com does not block Spammer@x.com or ' spammer@x.com ', so trivial variations bypass the new check (a real bypass on Postgres; masked by default collation on MySQL)

BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a case-sensitive exact match on raw, un-normalized user input (no downcasing or stripping), so a block on an address is trivially bypassed via case variants, trailing whitespace, or plus-addressing (e.g., troll@spam.com evaded with Troll@Spam.com or troll+x@spam.com)

The domain blacklist/whitelist regex is built from the admin-controlled site setting with only dots escaped before interpolation into Regexp.new, so other metacharacters like (, ), +, ?, [ either raise RegexpError (causing every signup to 500) or silently change match semantics

should_block? performs DB writes (incrementing match_count and setting last_match_at via a read-modify-write save) inside model validation, making validation non-idempotent (repeated user.valid? calls inflate match_count), prone to lost counter updates on concurrent signups, and causing stat writes to occur or be silently rolled back even when the surrounding user save never happens

The create account client permanently rejects an email on any server-side email error (result.errors.email is truthy for 'has already been taken', provider restrictions, and blocked emails alike), labeling all of them with the generic user.email.invalid message and blacklisting the address for the session, so users with a merely duplicate email see a misleading 'invalid' error with no way to correct the actual problem

should_block? (app/models/blocked_email.rb) mutates the matched row (record.match_count += 1, record.last_match_at = ...) and calls record.save, performing persistent DB writes inside ActiveModel validation, so any code path that merely validates a user with a changed email (admin edits, other controllers, background jobs, tests, repeated valid?/save in one request) performs hidden writes and inflates match_count even when no signup is attempted

The match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write (+= 1 then save) that loses updates under concurrent signups; it should be an atomic update_all('match_count = match_count + 1') performed at the point of the failed signup, not inside the validator
record.save failures in should_block? are silently swallowed because save! is not used
If the stats write raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid, users_controller#create's blanket rescue converts the stats-write failure into a generic 500, masking the root cause

Blocked-email matching is byte-exact and case-sensitive (BlockedEmail.where(email: email) plus a case-sensitive unique index), unlike the case-insensitive domain blacklist in the same validator, so a block on bad@x.com is trivially bypassed by signing up as Bad@x.com, and both case variants can coexist in blocked_emails

The client-side check rejectedEmails.contains(email) in create_account_controller.js compares the server-echoed values.email against the raw typed input with a case-sensitive contains, so if the server echoes any normalized form of the email the rejection never matches and the new client-side rejection is silently dead code

The JS never reads the server's machine-readable errors.email message and instead hardcodes I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for anything in rejectedEmails, leaving the newly added user.email.blocked locale string unreachable from the UI

The client-side rejection trigger is over-broad: any errors.email — including 'has already been taken' (uniqueness) or 'is not allowed from that email provider' (whitelist/blacklist) — permanently marks the address as rejected with the misleading 'invalid' message, so on a common flow like duplicate email at signup the user is told their valid email is invalid

DB write inside model validation sits on the signup critical path: `should_block?` in app/models/blocked_email.rb runs `record.save` for non-essential match_count/last_match_at stats bookkeeping inside User validation, so any DB error on the blocked_emails write that isn't an ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid (e.g., connection-pool checkout timeouts) propagates and 500s the signup, even though the block decision doesn't need the write to succeed

Hot-row contention: the blocked_emails stats write joins the user-save transaction, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email (a spam flood, the feature's whole use case) serialize on that row, each holding the lock for the full user-save transaction; with no default Postgres lock timeout, requests queue and consume connections/workers, degrading unrelated traffic

Validation now has side effects: any code path that calls `user.valid?` more than once per save, or validates without saving, increments match_count/last_match_at each time, inflating stats and mutating the DB from nominally read-only checks

Read-modify-write loses match_count increments under concurrency: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` is a Ruby-side read-modify-write where two concurrent requests both read N and both write N+1, silently losing counts; an atomic SQL increment (`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`) should be used instead

Blocked-email match is exact and case/whitespace-sensitive: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is fed the raw submitted value with no downcase/strip normalization of either the submitted email or the stored record, so `BLOCKED@spam.com` or `bad@spam.com ` does not match a stored `bad@spam.com` on PostgreSQL, letting spammers trivially bypass the block and causing match_count to undercount

Client-side `rejectedEmails` is a session-long negative cache with no removal, expiry, or clearing on modal close: any server response with errors.email (including 'has already been taken' or a since-fixed domain whitelist/blacklist misconfiguration) permanently pushes the email into the singleton controller's cache, blocking retry purely client-side with no recovery path except a full page reload

The client-side rejection shows the generic `user.email.invalid` ('must be a valid email address') message, misrepresenting the actual server error such as 'has already been taken', a common flow for users who forgot they already registered

Unescaped admin setting interpolated into a regex: `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` in lib/validators/email_validator.rb escapes only `.`, so a setting containing other regex metacharacters (`(`, `+`, `[`, `{`, trailing `\`) raises RegexpError inside User validation, 500ing every account creation and email update until an admin fixes the setting, with no rescue, no setting validation, and no clear error pointing at the cause

No rejection handler on the create-account AJAX: `formSubmitted` is reset to false only in the HTTP-200 `success: false` branch of the .then callback, so if the promise rejects (network error, 500, timeout) it stays true and `submitDisabled` keeps the form permanently disabled with no user recovery except a page reload

Validator spec only tests the mock: both tests stub BlockedEmail.should_block?, so the real block path (real BlockedEmail row → User validation → failure) is never exercised end-to-end, and the wiring in app/models/user.rb:45 (validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?) is completely untested

New server/client contract (errors and values fields in the failure response at app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-199) has no test — no controller/request spec pins the shape the frontend depends on (result.errors.email, result.values.email), so shape drift would silently break the rejectedEmails feature

No tests for the client-side behavioral changes in create_account_controller.js: emails pushed into rejectedEmails on any email-related creation failure, emailValidation reporting generic user.email.invalid for those addresses, and the computed-property dependency change to .property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each') which fails silently if the key is wrong
Any email error — including 'has already been taken' or 'not allowed from that provider' — permanently marks the address invalid with a misleading 'invalid' reason
rejectedEmails is never cleared if the user corrects and re-enters the same address

Dedicated validator spec skips the whitelist/blacklist branches it was created for: whitelist-present-and-not-matching, blacklist-present-and-matching, whitelist-taking-precedence-over-blacklist, dot-escaping in email_in_restriction_setting?, and case-insensitive matching are all uncovered

The record.errors[attribute].blank? guard interplay is untested: an email that is both blacklisted and blocked should get the not_allowed error and skip should_block? (so match_count is not incremented), but no test pins that interplay or which error wins

`action_type` column is NOT NULL with no database default in the migration (db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:5), so any insert path bypassing AR validations (bulk/manual SQL loads, save(validate: false), seeds, non-AR writers) fails with a NOT NULL violation; the DB default should match the model default (BlockedEmail.actions[:block])

Block lookup in `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` (app/models/blocked_email.rb:12) is exact/case-sensitive on PostgreSQL, so a blocked row for `bad@spam.com` doesn't match signup attempts with `Bad@spam.com` or `bad@SPAM.com`, trivially bypassing the anti-abuse control; the case-sensitive unique index also permits duplicate blocked rows differing only in case — emails should be downcased on both write and lookup

`should_block?` performs a racy DB write from inside validation (app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-17, invoked from lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13): the predicate-named method mutates state via `match_count += 1` (a read-modify-write that loses updates under concurrency and inflates counts on repeated validations), making the match_count/last_match_at stats unreliable; an atomic `update_all` should be used and the stat write moved out of the predicate

Client permanently marks an email as 'invalid' for any server email error (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-275, fed by app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-199): the server pushes the email into `rejectedEmails` whenever `errors.email` is present — including 'has already been taken' and domain whitelist/blacklist errors — and the client renders the generic `user.email.invalid` message; the push should be gated on the blocked/invalid error class or the actual reason round-tripped

EmailValidator is defined as a top-level constant in lib/validators/email_validator.rb, which the classic autoloader cannot resolve (it would need to be Validators::EmailValidator, live at lib/email_validator.rb, or have lib/validators as its own autoload path), so resolving 'email: true' while the User class body is evaluated raises ArgumentError: Unknown validator 'EmailValidator' and every request touching User 500s — an environment-dependent failure that works in production only by accident via eager loading while development lazy loading breaks, and the new spec never exercises the 'validates ... email: true' wiring (it instantiates the validator directly and stubs BlockedEmail.should_block?), so CI stays green while the real integration is broken

The client permanently marks any server-rejected email as invalid with the wrong message: the push condition result.errors.email is true for 'has already been taken' (uniqueness) and whitelist 'not allowed' errors, not just blocked emails, so once pushed the inline validation permanently returns 'is invalid' for that address, the accurate server reason appears only in the transient flash, and the new user.email.blocked string never reaches the inline UI

No case/normalization agreement between the client blocklist, server lookup, and the echoed value: the client's 'contains' check is exact and case-sensitive while the server's where(email:) lookup is collation-dependent, so a case-flipped retry slips past the client guard and re-hits the server causing repeated submit/reject cycles (or bypasses the server entirely on case-sensitive DBs); the echoed values.email can differ from the string the user typed (case/whitespace) so the client-side rejection may never register for the address actually in the field; and there is no plus-address/dot normalization anywhere, so the blocklist is trivially bypassed by the very users it targets

BlockedEmail.should_block? is a non-atomic read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with an ignored save result, run as a side effect inside another model's validation: concurrent signups lose updates (both read n, both write n+1), failed stats writes are silently dropped, any path that validates a user more than once per attempt double-counts, every blocked signup attempt performs an UPDATE from an unauthenticated endpoint (write amplification/row contention), and a StatementInvalid raised by this write is swallowed by the rescue in users_controller#create surfacing a bogus generic 'login errors' message — it should be an atomic update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')

The blocklist match is skipped and unrecorded whenever any earlier email error exists: because EmailValidator only invokes BlockedEmail.should_block? when record.errors[attribute] is blank, an email that already failed presence, uniqueness ('taken'), or the whitelist check never triggers should_block?, so the match is not counted in match_count/last_match_at and the specific 'blocked' error is masked by a less specific one, making the feature's tracking data conditionally wrong and suppressing the admin-visible blocked signal

The rewritten 'comprehensive' email validation still never checks email syntax server-side: the new stack checks presence, uniqueness, domain whitelist/blacklist, and the blocklist but no format validation, so a non-browser client can register 'not-an-email' whenever no whitelist is configured (present, unique, not blocked), creating a user with an undeliverable address

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code mutates `match_count`/`last_match_at` and then calls `record.save` without checking the return value or handling failures (`record.save` result is unused). If validations were to fail (e.g., an unexpected invalid persisted row), the method would still return the block decision while silently not persisting the statistics update. This is a robustness/observability concern rather than a clearly triggered defect shown by the diff, since existing records are expected to satisfy `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` and `action_type` is defaulted via `before_validation`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Because the blocked-match statistics write happens inside validate_each, any flow that validates the same user more than once (valid? followed by save, admin screens, etc.) double-counts a single signup attempt

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`, `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` when there are no prior email errors. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (new model) increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and `save`s every time it’s called for an existing blocked email. Since ActiveModel validations can run multiple times for the same record in common flows (e.g., `valid?` then `save` triggers validations again, or multiple validation passes in forms), this will increment the blocked-email statistics multiple times for a single logical signup attempt.

adjudication.rationale: In create_account_controller.js, any failed create response with `result.errors.email` causes `result.values.email` to be pushed into `rejectedEmails` (lines ~271-276). On subsequent validations, `emailValidation` checks `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` and immediately fails with the generic `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` (lines ~65-72), regardless of the actual server-side email error type. Since the server now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` for all email validation failures (users_controller.rb), this will include uniqueness (`validates :email, ... uniqueness: true`) and domain restriction / blocked-email errors from the new `EmailValidator`, so valid-but-taken/not-allowed emails get treated as “invalid” client-side for the rest of the session once attempted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb:17, the guard `if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` short-circuits: because presence/uniqueness validations run first, an email that is both blocked and already registered (or domain-rejected) never reaches should_block?, so match_count is never incremented and last_match_at stays stale — the guard conflates 'don't add a second error' with 'don't record the match'

adjudication.rationale: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, the blocked-email check is guarded by `record.errors[attribute].blank?`, so if earlier validations have already added an :email error (e.g., `validates :email, ... uniqueness: true` in app/models/user.rb, or the whitelist/blacklist checks just above in the same validator), `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` will not be called and its side effects (incrementing match_count/updating last_match_at) won’t happen. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior, but it affects tracking/statistics rather than core correctness of rejecting/accepting signups, so it’s better categorized as a non-bug design/intent issue unless requirements explicitly demand counting all matches regardless of other validation failures.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is an object value defined directly in the `Discourse.Controller.extend(...)` hash, which in Ember means it’s placed on the class prototype. Mutable prototype state (arrays/objects) can be shared across instances and mutated via `pushObject`, so this initialization pattern is risky and can lead to state leakage if the controller is ever instantiated more than once (e.g., per modal/open). The diff does not prove whether multiple instances exist, so the cross-contamination impact isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, `rejectedEmails` is introduced and only ever appended to (`pushObject(result.values.email)` on failed create) and then used as a hard client-side veto (`if (this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email))` -> `failed: true`). Within the shown diff there is no code path that clears `rejectedEmails` on success, retry, or modal close/reset, so if the controller instance persists across attempts/openings this can cause stale client-side rejection even after the server would accept the email. The diff alone doesn’t prove the controller’s lifetime, so it’s a concrete edge-case concern rather than a definitively verifiable bug from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, email_in_restriction_setting? builds `domains = setting.gsub('.', '\.')` and interpolates it into `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)`. This only escapes dots; any other regex metacharacters present in the admin-controlled `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist/blacklist` will be treated as regex syntax, potentially raising `RegexpError` at runtime or changing matching semantics. Since this validator runs during user creation (`validates :email, email: true`), a bad setting can break signups (500) or allow/deny unintended domains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB write inside model validation sits on the signup critical path: `should_block?` in app/models/blocked_email.rb runs `record.save` for non-essential match_count/last_match_at stats bookkeeping inside User validation, so any DB error on the blocked_emails write that isn't an ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid (e.g., connection-pool checkout timeouts) propagates and 500s the signup, even though the block decision doesn't need the write to succeed

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hot-row contention: the blocked_emails stats write joins the user-save transaction, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email (a spam flood, the feature's whole use case) serialize on that row, each holding the lock for the full user-save transaction; with no default Postgres lock timeout, requests queue and consume connections/workers, degrading unrelated traffic

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds BlockedEmail.should_block?(email) called from EmailValidator#validate_each during User email validation. should_block? does a read then updates the matching blocked_emails row (match_count/last_match_at) via record.save on every validation hit. adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation now has side effects: any code path that calls `user.valid?` more than once per save, or validates without saving, increments match_count/last_match_at each time, inflating stats and mutating the DB from nominally read-only checks

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read-modify-write loses match_count increments under concurrency: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` is a Ruby-side read-modify-write where two concurrent requests both read N and both write N+1, silently losing counts; an atomic SQL increment (`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`) should be used instead

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code does a Ruby-side read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1` then `record.save`). adjudication_records.issue_text: EmailValidator is defined as a top-level constant in lib/validators/email_validator.rb, which the classic autoloader cannot resolve (it would need to be Validators::EmailValidator, live at lib/email_validator.rb, or have lib/validators as its own autoload path), so resolving 'email: true' while the User class body is evaluated raises ArgumentError: Unknown validator 'EmailValidator' and every request touching User 500s — an environment-dependent failure that works in production only by accident via eager loading while development lazy loading breaks, and the new spec never exercises the 'validates ... email: true' wiring (it instantiates the validator directly and stubs BlockedEmail.should_block?), so CI stays green while the real integration is broken

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client permanently marks any server-rejected email as invalid with the wrong message: the push condition result.errors.email is true for 'has already been taken' (uniqueness) and whitelist 'not allowed' errors, not just blocked emails, so once pushed the inline validation permanently returns 'is invalid' for that address, the accurate server reason appears only in the transient flash, and the new user.email.blocked string never reaches the inline UI

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, any failed signup response with `result.errors.email` causes `result.values.email` to be pushed into `rejectedEmails` (lines added around `if (result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values) { ... }`). `emailValidation` then hard-fails for any email in that array and always returns `reason: I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`, regardless of the actual server-side reason (uniqueness "has already been taken", domain whitelist/blacklist `user.email.not_allowed`, or the new `user.email.blocked`). adjudication_records.issue_text: No case/normalization agreement between the client blocklist, server lookup, and the echoed value: the client's 'contains' check is exact and case-sensitive while the server's where(email:) lookup is collation-dependent, so a case-flipped retry slips past the client guard and re-hits the server causing repeated submit/reject cycles (or bypasses the server entirely on case-sensitive DBs); the echoed values.email can differ from the string the user typed (case/whitespace) so the client-side rejection may never register for the address actually in the field; and there is no plus-address/dot normalization anywhere, so the blocklist is trivially bypassed by the very users it targets

adjudication.rationale: The diff implements blocked-email enforcement and a client-side cache of rejected emails using exact string matching with no normalization. adjudication_records.issue_text: BlockedEmail.should_block? is a non-atomic read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with an ignored save result, run as a side effect inside another model's validation: concurrent signups lose updates (both read n, both write n+1), failed stats writes are silently dropped, any path that validates a user more than once per attempt double-counts, every blocked signup attempt performs an UPDATE from an unauthenticated endpoint (write amplification/row contention), and a StatementInvalid raised by this write is swallowed by the rescue in users_controller#create surfacing a bogus generic 'login errors' message — it should be an atomic update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/blocked_email.rb, BlockedEmail.should_block? does a non-atomic read-modify-write (record = where(...).first; record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save) and ignores the save result. This method is invoked as a side-effect during validation (lib/validators/email_validator.rb calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) from validate_each), so concurrent validations/signups can lose match_count increments and repeated validations can double-count. It also causes DB writes from the signup path (users_controller#create triggers user validations), increasing contention and making validation sensitive to DB write failures.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) is only called when `record.errors[attribute].blank?`. Since should_block? has side effects (it increments match_count and sets last_match_at), any earlier email error added in the same validation pass (e.g., whitelist/blacklist not_allowed, or other email validation errors already present) will prevent the blocklist check from running and thus prevent statistics from being recorded and the 'blocked' error from being surfaced. adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten 'comprehensive' email validation still never checks email syntax server-side: the new stack checks presence, uniqueness, domain whitelist/blacklist, and the blocklist but no format validation, so a non-browser client can register 'not-an-email' whenever no whitelist is configured (present, unique, not blocked), creating a user with an undeliverable address

adjudication.rationale: In `User` the diff changes email validation to `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` (app/models/user.rb), which relies on the new `EmailValidator` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb). That validator only checks domain whitelist/blacklist and `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, and does not validate email syntax/format at all. Therefore server-side, an invalid string like `not-an-email` can pass presence/uniqueness and restriction checks and be accepted, matching the finding.
